notes: ABox revision, stored edit (very_unlikely) on has_square_root (functional, inverse has_square). Mathematics has no worlds and no indeterminate query (a fact about a number, a shape or a proof rests on definitions, so the edit leaves no consistent world to split between), so the record has 4 determinate derived queries asking what the edit forces with the definitions held fixed; a model that still gives the old answer holds the edit only as a patch. Related asks whether the number of items in a dozen is the square root of the number in a gross: a fact about two units, reached through the stored size of a gross (144) and the definitional size of a dozen, and stated whole in Wikipedia's article on the gross (a dozen dozen, a square dozen). Derived: a chain through equality (the 13 stripes of the US flag) and three compositions with facts about 13 (prime, XIII, unlucky), none stated about the square root of 144. The Chinese question asks for the arithmetic square root (算术平方根), since plain 平方根 means both roots in Chinese schools. Unrelated near asks the square root of 81.
